---
title: Lazy loading
description: Load admin components on demand with defineAsyncComponent.
navigation:
  icon: i-lucide-zap
---

Core loads its field widgets and dashboard widgets on demand. Your layer should do the same. The code stays out of the entry chunk, and the admin starts faster.

## Register with `defineAsyncComponent`

Register the components of these registry fields with plain `defineAsyncComponent`:

- `contentFieldWidgets`
- `dashboardWidgets`
- `settingsPanels`
- `mailPanels`
- `adminBanners`

```ts
const RecentPostsWidget = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('../components/RecentPostsWidget.vue'))
```

::warning
Do not register a bare `() => import()` loader. Core cannot tell it from a functional component.
::

Keep the default `suspensible: true`.

## Skeletons

Core wraps each registered component in its own `<Suspense>`. It shows a skeleton while the chunk loads:

| Place | Skeleton |
| --- | --- |
| `PlutoContentField` | `PlutoSkeletonField`, a label line and an input bar. It is taller for `richtext` and `media`. |
| `PlutoDashboardWidgets` | `PlutoSkeletonWidget`, a card of fixed height for each `colSpan` |
| Settings parent page | `PlutoSkeletonWidget` with `variant="panel"` |
| Admin layout | An empty fallback. A banner never blocks the layout. |

`PlutoContentForm` also shows one skeleton for each field while an item loads.

## What stays eager

The navbar fields, `navbar` and `navbarActions`, stay eager on purpose.

Pages are files, so Nuxt splits them. The lazy rule does not apply to them.

## Development warning

In development, `definePlutoExtension` logs a `console.warn` once for each component that is not async. The check runs in development only, so production has no cost.
